title: Code Reviewer workflow, version 1
description: A workflow is a JSON document (#833, agent workflows, app/src/workflows/, docs/workflows.md): one or more triggers and a list of steps that run in order. Five kinds of node: the trigger, the agent step, the action, the control nodes `if` and `loop`, and (reserved) the workflow as a step. Nodes talk to each other only through values: a text may hold `{{step.field}}` references to what an earlier step yielded. The schema states the form, closed everywhere: a key it does not name is refused. What it cannot state is checked by the validator, which also gives every problem a JSON pointer, a stable code, the cause and the names that were available: that every reference points at a step that ran before on every path, the types of the values that flow, the ids, limits, and that profiles and environments exist. A workflow has several triggers (#916), each with pre-steps of its own; when one fires, its pre-steps run and then the shared steps, so the shared steps read only what every trigger yields. A run works on ONE repository: the one of its trigger (the ticket's: `trigger.ticket.repo` of a label trigger and of a manual or api trigger with a `ticket` input, the input `repo` of a manual one), so a node names none. The single `trigger` of format 1 before #916 is still read, as a list of one trigger without pre-steps; `github.issueLabeled` is read as `ticket.labeled`. The inputs that decide a TARGET (the issue, the branches, the labels, the environment) take a literal or one whole reference to a value the platform or the caller vouches for (the issue or ticket number, the default branch, an input of a manual trigger, the branch of an agent step), never a value an agent reported and never the title, body or labels of the issue, which whoever opened it wrote: the validator holds them to it (`target_from_untrusted_value`). A reader ignores nothing: unknown fields are errors. `forEach`, `approval` and `workflow` are named here so a document can use them later; version 1 refuses them (code `kind_not_supported`). Written by the app (src/workflows/); the version is in the path and in `version`.

trigger.description: The single trigger of format 1 before #916, read as a list of one trigger without pre-steps.

triggers.description: The triggers that start the workflow, one to ten, each with pre-steps of its own. A workflow has `triggers` or the single `trigger` of the older form, not both.

budgetUsd.description: What the workflow may spend in USD over all its steps; 20 when left out, and not above the operator's maximum (the validator).

turnTimeLimitMinutes.description: How long one agent turn of the workflow may run, in whole minutes (#918): 15 to 60, 60 when left out (the Dispatcher stops an Implementer VM at 3600 seconds). A turn that is still running at the limit is cut. The cost of a turn is not set here: it is capped by what is left of `budgetUsd`.

mcp.description: The MCP servers of the workspace the lane's agents may use (#1052, epic #1049): the ids of servers of the MCP page. Left out: none. A step may narrow the list (`mcp` of an agent step). That a server exists in the workspace, and that a step names only servers of its lane, is the validator's (`mcp_server_unknown`, `mcp_server_not_in_lane`).

onFailure.description: Steps that run once after the run ended `failed` or `cancelled` (the old stop), never after `succeeded` and never when a member discards the run (#902, #921). The run keeps its final status. The form is that of `steps`; the validator holds them to comments (`ticket.comment`, `pullRequest.comment`, `github.issue.comment`), label changes (`ticket.labels`, `github.issue.labels`) and `if` over them (`on_failure_step_not_allowed`), gives them `{{failure.status}}`, `{{failure.stepId}}`, `{{failure.code}}` and `{{failure.message}}` and none of the steps above, and counts them against the 50 steps of the document.

Template.description: A text; `{{step.field}}` in it is replaced by the value of that field when the step runs. `{{step.field | default <JSON>}}` gives a value for a field that may be missing. `\{{` is a literal `{{`.

Reference.description: A text that is exactly one reference and nothing else (no text and no space around it), where a number, true/false or a list is wanted: the value keeps its type. The `default` of a reference may hold braces nested three deep and JSON strings that hold `}}`. The pattern is `REFERENCE_PATTERN` of src/workflows/template.ts.

profile.description: A profile, `name` for the newest version or `name@version` to pin one. Deprecated (ADR 0007, #1105): a step either names a profile or carries its settings itself (`harness`, `model`, `canPush`, `instructions`, `setupScript`, `network`, `runner`), never both (`profile_with_inline_settings`) and never neither (`agent_settings_required`; both are the validator's, the schema allows either).

harness.description: #1105 (ADR 0007), settings of the step itself, instead of `profile`: the harness the agent runs with. `opencode` when left out; `claude-code` exists only on a runner (`harness_needs_runner`) and takes `model` `{"provider": "claude-code", "model": "<name>"}`.

model.description: #1105, settings of the step itself: the model, as a profile held it. `{"entryId"}` is a released catalog entry (the platform's key; not on a runner, `runner_needs_own_key`), `{"provider", "model"}` a model of the workspace's own key (what a runner works with). Required with the other settings; whether the workspace can run it is the validator's (`model_not_allowed`).

canPush.description: #1105, settings of the step itself: whether the step may push branches. Required with the other settings: decide it. It decides whether the step yields `branch`, `commits`, `headCommit` and `pushed`, and whether its token can write.

instructions.description: #1105, settings of the step itself: the standing system-level text of the agent (1 to 20,000 characters), appended last and unchanged, so the prompt cache hits across turns. Not `instruction`, which is the task of this round.

setupScript.description: #1105 (ADR 0007, decision 11), settings of the step itself: the script the runner runs once before the agent starts, in the agent's own container (at most 64 KB of UTF-8, kept as written). For a step on a hosted runner and, since #1126, on a self-hosted one (on the harness `claude-code` the script ends before the login is handed to the agent). Not with `profile` (the environment of the profile holds its own).

network.description: #1105 (ADR 0007, decision 11), settings of the step itself: the rule for the agent's network, as the environment held it: `off` (the default), `list` (the exact or `*.suffix` host names in `hosts`, at least one) or `open`; `hosts` only with `list`. For a step on a hosted or a self-hosted runner. On the harness `claude-code` `open` is refused (`subscription_network_open`), a `*.suffix` entry on a domain anybody can get a subdomain of is refused (`subscription_network_wildcard`) and the listed hosts are only read (GET and HEAD) beside the model's own host. Not with `profile`.

runner.description: #1105 (ADR 0007, decisions 6, 14 and 16), a setting of the step itself: the **id** of the concrete runner the agent runs on: a hosted runner (one type of the provided Vercel Sandbox, such as "Vercel Sandbox 4 vCPU", a fixed size) or a self-hosted runner of the workspace. A literal: where the agent works is a target, so version 1 takes no reference (`target_from_untrusted_value`). The id, not the name: a rename changes the name and no id, so no lane. An id of no runner of the workspace, or of a revoked runner, is `runner_unknown` (`available` lists the ids). A step with settings of its own names this or an `environment`, never both (`runner_with_environment`) and never neither (`runner_required`). Not with `profile` (a profile says where it works).

environment.description: Deprecated (#919): leave it out, the step runs in the environment of its profile. A step with settings of its own (no `profile`) may name its environment here instead of a `runner`, in release A, for documents written before the runner (`runner_required` when it names neither; `runner_with_environment` when it names both). The name of an environment of the workspace, as a literal: it decides where the agent works, so version 1 takes no reference (`target_from_untrusted_value`, checked by the validator). When the profile names an environment, this must be that one (`environment_mismatch`); a profile version saved before #919 names none and needs it (`environment_required`).

instruction.description: The task. A loop body may give `first` (round one) and `next` (later rounds, where `{{previous.<step>.<field>}}` is available).

session.description: `new` (default) or the session of an earlier agent step, or of this step itself in the round before.

branch.description: The branch a session of its own starts from, instead of the base branch of the run: a literal, `{{trigger.repo.defaultBranch}}`, an input of a manual trigger or `{{<agent step>.branch}}` (the branch of an earlier agent step that may push). A target, so no other reference (`target_from_untrusted_value`); not with `session.continue` (checked by the validator: a session that goes on keeps its branch).

repos.description: #1091 (epic #1090, ADR 0006): the repositories this step works on, one to ten. Left out, the step works on the run's one repository on a branch of its own, exactly as before (and the `branch` above applies). With `repos`, each entry names a repository of the workspace (any active one the GitHub App can reach, and write to when the profile may push), its base branch and, optionally, the branch to work on: a branch that exists is checked out and continued, one that does not is created from the base, and an entry without a branch works and pushes directly on its base branch. The run's repository is not special and need not be listed. Not together with `branch` (`repos_with_branch`) and not with `session.continue` (`repos_with_session_continue`): a session that goes on keeps the repositories of the session it continues, as the first turn resolved them (`name`, `base`, `branch` are never resolved again, also for an answer turn or a resume). `{{<step>.repos}}` of a step that continues a session yields the session's list. Two entries may not name the same repository, **compared without regard to case** (`Acme/App` and `acme/app` are one repository on GitHub): `repo_duplicate`, which the validator reports for two literals that are equal in that sense and the engine for the filled-in references when the step runs, before the agent starts (free). Two repositories whose mount names (`ImplementerMountName` in `runner-api.v1.json`) clash after the derivation end the step `repo_name_clash` (free). Version 1 documents without `repos` are unchanged.

result.description: What the agent's result looks like; the finish tool is made from it. Without one the step yields the facts only (and the result schema of the profile, once profiles bring one).

mcp.description: The MCP servers this step may use (#1052): a subset of the lane's `mcp`. Left out: all of the lane's. An empty list: none. A server the lane does not name is `mcp_server_not_in_lane` (checked by the validator).

allOf.description: #1105: a step that names no `profile` but has any of the settings of its own needs `model` and `canPush`. (Neither a profile nor any setting, or both, is the validator's: `agent_settings_required`, `profile_with_inline_settings`.)
#1091: `repos` and the single start `branch` exclude each other.
#1091: `repos` and `session.continue` exclude each other: a session that goes on keeps its repositories.

ModelField.description: #1105: the id of a catalog entry, a provider slug or a model name in the settings of an agent step: one line, not only white space, 200 characters at most.

AgentStepRepo.description: #1091 (epic #1090): one repository of an agent step. All three fields decide what the agent works on and where its commits go, so they are targets: `repo` is a literal `owner/name` or exactly one reference to `{{trigger.ticket.repo.fullName}}`, `{{trigger.repo.fullName}}` or an input of a manual trigger; `base` is a literal branch name or exactly one reference to `{{trigger.ticket.repo.defaultBranch}}`, `{{trigger.repo.defaultBranch}}` or an input of a manual trigger; `branch` is a literal or a text whose references are only values the platform or the caller vouches for (`{{trigger.ticket.key}}`, `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`, `{{trigger.input.<name>}}`), so `feature/{{trigger.ticket.key}}` is valid. Nothing an agent or an issue's title, body or labels wrote (`target_from_untrusted_value`). A reference that gives something that is not a repository or a branch name fails the step before the agent starts (`repo_invalid`, `branch_invalid`).

repo.description: The repository, `owner/name`, as a literal or one reference. A repository the workspace has no active installation for is `repo_not_available` (checked when the step runs, free).

base.description: The branch the work starts from when `branch` does not exist, and the branch a pull request is opened against. Left out: the default branch of that repository, read when the step runs. A base branch the repository does not have ends the step `base_branch_not_found` (free).

branch.description: The branch to work on. It exists: it is checked out and the work continues on it (a second fix round, a retry). It does not exist: it is created from the head of `base`. Left out, or equal to `base`: the agent works directly on the base branch and what it commits is pushed to it (a branch protection rule may refuse that; the refusal is reported for that repository, never forced). A pull request needs a branch different from the base.

connector.description: `pullRequest.open` is the provider-neutral name of `github.pullRequest.open` (#917); saved lanes keep the old name.

head.description: A branch: a literal, or exactly one reference to the branch of an agent step that may push (`{{implement.branch}}`). The validator refuses anything else.

repos.description: #1094 (epic #1090, ADR 0006): exactly one reference to the `repos` fact of an earlier agent step that may push (`{{implement.repos}}`); the validator refuses anything else (`target_from_untrusted_value`). Replaces `head` and `base`: opens one pull request for each entry whose branch differs from its base, has commits ahead of the base on the provider and has no open pull request from that branch yet, in that entry's repository against its base (an open one is reported as `existing`). An entry with direct work (branch equal to base), nothing pushed or no commits ahead is skipped, not an error. `title` and `body` apply to every pull request, and `{{repo.fullName}}`, `{{repo.base}}` and `{{repo.branch}}` stand for the repository being opened in them. The step yields `pullRequests` (one entry per repository: `fullName`, `base`, `head`, `state` opened|existing|skipped, `reason` for a skipped one, `number` and `url`) and the single `number`, `url`, `existing` and `repository` of the first pull request that exists (absent when none does). `ticket.requestReview` asks for the first pull request only, in its own repository (`repository` of the step output: `{{pr.repository}}`); it skips when there is none. The `reason` of a skipped one is `direct`, `not_pushed`, `push_rejected` or `no_commits`.

base.description: A branch: a literal, or exactly one reference to `{{trigger.repo.defaultBranch}}` or to an input of a manual trigger (`{{trigger.input.<name>}}`). The default branch of the repository when left out. The validator refuses anything else.

allOf.description: #1094: a pull request step names the branch to open it from (`head`) or the repositories (`repos`).

PullRequestInput.description: A pull request: a positive whole number up to 2147483647, or exactly one reference to the number of a pull request an earlier `pullRequest.open` (or `github.pullRequest.open`) action opened (`{{<step id>.number}}`) or to an input of a manual trigger that is declared `integer`. The validator refuses anything else (`target_from_untrusted_value`), and the engine checks the number again when it runs.

board.description: The GitHub Project (projects_v2) of the repository's owner that holds the board: its number ("7") or its node id ("PVT_…"). A literal, no reference (`target_from_untrusted_value`; `invalid_value` for another form). Optional (#922): left out, the board of the project the lane belongs to is used; named, it overrides that board.

status.description: The name of an option of the board's Status field, as the board spells it: a literal, no reference. The engine looks it up when the step runs and ends the step with `board_status_unknown`, naming the options the board has, when there is none of that name.

repository.description: #1094: the repository of the pull request as `owner/name`, when it is not the repository of the run: a literal, or exactly one reference to `{{<step id>.repository}}` of a `pullRequest.open` step with `repos` (the repository of its first pull request). Only an active repository of the workspace is acted on. Left out, the review is asked in the repository of the run. When the number has no value because that step opened no pull request, the step skips (`skipped: "no_pull_request"`); a `| default` on that number is refused.

reviewers.description: The text "project members" (the members of the project that has a GitHub login; the ones that cannot review this pull request are left out), or a list of GitHub logins (literals and references to inputs of a manual trigger, one reference per entry), or exactly one reference to a list input. `invalid_value` names "project members" in `available` for another text.

IssueInput.description: A positive whole number up to 2147483647, or exactly one reference to the issue of the trigger (`{{trigger.issue}}`, `{{trigger.issue.number}}`, `{{trigger.ticket}}`, `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`) or to an input of a manual trigger that is declared `integer`. The default of a reference is held to the same rule. The validator refuses the title, body and labels of the issue, and the engine checks the number again when it runs.

LabelsInput.description: Label names: a list of literals and references to inputs of a manual trigger (`{{trigger.input.<name>}}`, one reference per entry), or exactly one reference to a list input. The title, body and labels of the issue, and an agent's result, are data and are not taken (`target_from_untrusted_value`). An action may not add the label that starts the workflow (`label_retriggers_workflow`).

maxRounds.description: At most this many rounds, 1 to 10. The loop ends earlier when `until` holds (exit `until`) or when the workflow budget is used up between two rounds (exit `budget`). Afterwards `{{<loop id>.exit}}` is `until`, `maxRounds` or `budget` and `{{<loop id>.rounds}}` the number of rounds that ran; the steps of the body keep the values of the last round.

ReservedStep.description: Reserved: `forEach`, `approval` and a workflow as a step are named so a document can use them in a later version. Version 1 refuses them (`kind_not_supported`); their other fields are not defined yet.

Operand.description: A reference like "{{review.findings}}", a text, a number or true/false.

Condition.description: Exactly one operator. `empty`/`notEmpty` ask whether a list or text is empty; `equals`/`notEquals` compare two texts, numbers or true/false values; `all`, `any`, `not` combine. Nested four levels deep at most (the validator).

ManualTriggerEntry.description: Started by hand (`manual`) or through the API (`api`; the start form offers `manual` only). `input` declares what the caller hands in; steps read it as `{{trigger.input.<field>}}`. Without `input` the trigger takes no fields and its run works on the repository of the lane's project (the lane must belong to a project). A run works on one repository: an input that is declared may declare `ticket` (type `ticket`, required: a reference like `github:owner/repo#128`; the run works in the repository of the ticket and steps read it as `{{trigger.ticket.number|title|body|labels|type|assignees|url|repo|repo.defaultBranch}}`) or `repo`, a required text (owner/name); one that declares neither works, like a trigger without `input`, on the repository of the lane's project. The schema cannot say it (`repo_required`).

TicketLabeledTriggerEntry.description: Started when the label is put on a ticket (an issue of a repository of the workspace). Steps read `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels`, `.type`, `.assignees`, `.repo` and, as workflows written before #916 do, `{{trigger.issue.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels` and `{{trigger.repo.fullName}}`, `.owner`, `.name`, `.defaultBranch`. `github.issueLabeled` is the old name of `ticket.labeled`.

label.description: The label that starts the workflow. Two `ticket.labeled` triggers of one workflow may not wait for the same label, in any case (`duplicate_trigger_label`: the schema cannot say it, the validator does).

TicketStatusChangedTriggerEntry.description: Started when a ticket is moved into the status `to` (#1036), whoever moved it, the factory's own moves included. The status names are the provider's own (GitHub: the options of the Status field of the project's board). Steps read `{{trigger.ticket.…}}` as for `ticket.labeled` and `{{trigger.status.from}}`, `{{trigger.status.to}}` (`from` is empty when the ticket had no status). A workflow that moves a ticket into its own `to` starts itself again: the validator warns (`status_retriggers_workflow`).

to.description: The status that starts the workflow, as the provider names it.

from.description: Optional: only a move out of this status starts the workflow.

PullRequestPushedTriggerEntry.description: Reserved (#916): a push to a pull request. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

ScheduleTriggerEntry.description: Reserved (#916): a schedule, `cron` with five fields separated by one space. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

ManualTrigger.description: Started by hand (`manual`) or through the API (`api`; the start form offers `manual` only). `input` declares what the caller hands in; steps read it as `{{trigger.input.<field>}}`. Without `input` the trigger takes no fields and its run works on the repository of the lane's project (the lane must belong to a project). A run works on one repository: an input that is declared may declare `ticket` (type `ticket`, required: a reference like `github:owner/repo#128`; the run works in the repository of the ticket and steps read it as `{{trigger.ticket.number|title|body|labels|type|assignees|url|repo|repo.defaultBranch}}`) or `repo`, a required text (owner/name); one that declares neither works, like a trigger without `input`, on the repository of the lane's project. The schema cannot say it (`repo_required`).

TicketLabeledTrigger.description: Started when the label is put on a ticket (an issue of a repository of the workspace). Steps read `{{trigger.ticket.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels`, `.type`, `.assignees`, `.repo` and, as workflows written before #916 do, `{{trigger.issue.number}}`, `.title`, `.body`, `.url`, `.labels` and `{{trigger.repo.fullName}}`, `.owner`, `.name`, `.defaultBranch`. `github.issueLabeled` is the old name of `ticket.labeled`.

TicketStatusChangedTrigger.description: Started when a ticket is moved into the status `to` (#1036), whoever moved it, the factory's own moves included. The status names are the provider's own (GitHub: the options of the Status field of the project's board). Steps read `{{trigger.ticket.…}}` as for `ticket.labeled` and `{{trigger.status.from}}`, `{{trigger.status.to}}` (`from` is empty when the ticket had no status). A workflow that moves a ticket into its own `to` starts itself again: the validator warns (`status_retriggers_workflow`).

to.description: The status that starts the workflow, as the provider names it.

from.description: Optional: only a move out of this status starts the workflow.

PullRequestPushedTrigger.description: Reserved (#916): a push to a pull request. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

ScheduleTrigger.description: Reserved (#916): a schedule, `cron` with five fields separated by one space. The format validates it, the engine starts no run from it yet.

Trigger.description: The single trigger of the older form: the same kinds, without `id` and `steps`.

TriggerEntry.description: One entry of `triggers`: the same kinds, each with an `id` (unique among the triggers, the start API names it) and `steps`, the pre-steps that run first when this trigger started the run.

TriggerSteps.description: The pre-steps of a trigger: the form of `steps`, and may be empty. They see only the values of their own trigger; the shared steps after them see only what every trigger yields.

TriggerInput.description: The input of a manual or api trigger: a result schema (result-schema.v1.json) whose fields may also be `ticket`, a reference to a ticket like `github:owner/repo#128`. Only a field of the input itself may be a ticket, and it is called `ticket`.

TicketTarget.description: As `IssueInput`, for the action on a ticket: a positive whole number up to 2147483647, or exactly one reference to the ticket of the trigger (`{{trigger.ticket}}`, `{{trigger.ticket.number}}` (#1040: for a ticket of a platform that does not number its tickets, Jira, the action takes the text key `PROJ-12` of `{{trigger.ticket}}`), or the issue of a label trigger, `{{trigger.issue}}`) or to an input of a manual trigger that is declared `integer`. A trigger that does not yield a ticket makes the reference `reference_not_in_scope`.
